questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Every Friday evening, the Karoui family gathers in the kitchen. The parents prepare couscous, and the children set the table and tell jokes. Grandfather, who lives next door, always arrives first. For them, this weekly meal is more important than any present, because it keeps the family close."

What is the main idea of the text?

options.text: The family's weekly meal keeps them close together.
Couscous is the best dish to cook on a Friday evening.
Grandfather lives in the house next door.
Children should always help in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: The last sentence gives the message of the whole text: the weekly meal "keeps the family close", and every sentence describes that meal. Couscous and the house next door are details of one sentence each, and the text never says that children should always help — that is an opinion.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Every Friday evening, the Karoui family gathers in the kitchen. The parents prepare couscous, and the children set the table and tell jokes. Grandfather, who lives next door, always arrives first. For them, this weekly meal is more important than any present, because it keeps the family close."

In the last sentence, what does the word "it" refer to?
questions.explanation: "It keeps the family close": "it" is one thing, and the meaning shows that it is "this weekly meal". "any present" is only what the meal is compared with, Grandfather is a person (he), and it is the meal, not the Friday evening itself, that keeps the family close.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Every Friday evening, the Karoui family gathers in the kitchen. The parents prepare couscous, and the children set the table and tell jokes. Grandfather, who lives next door, always arrives first. For them, this weekly meal is more important than any present, because it keeps the family close."

Language: complete the sentence as it is in the text:

"For them, this weekly meal is ______ any present."
questions.explanation: "Important" is a long adjective, so its comparative is more + adjective + than: "more important than". The -er ending is only for short adjectives ("importanter" does not exist), "the most" is the superlative and never takes "than", and equality needs "as … as", not "as … than".

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Every Friday evening, the Karoui family gathers in the kitchen. The parents prepare couscous, and the children set the table and tell jokes. Grandfather, who lives next door, always arrives first. For them, this weekly meal is more important than any present, because it keeps the family close."

Language: in "Grandfather, who lives next door", what does the relative pronoun "who" refer to?
questions.explanation: "Who" is used for people and refers to the noun just before it: "Grandfather". The door and the kitchen are things (they would take "which"), and "the children" is plural and is not the noun the clause describes.

Writing: you want to add a sentence about another family activity. Which one best continues the paragraph?

options.text: The price of vegetables at the market has risen sharply this month.
My favourite football team won an important match last weekend.
After dinner, they often play cards together and laugh until late.
The new mobile phone in the shop window has a very good camera.

questions.explanation: A good continuation stays on the topic of the paragraph — a family that spends time together — and playing cards after dinner does exactly that. Vegetable prices, a football match and a new phone may be true, but they jump to another topic and break the unity of the paragraph.
